handback.t:
W17 (retrieval track R, round 3) is finished. The goal "no Holm-significant loss in control worlds while keeping the wins" is NOT met against the best fair baseline. It is met only against the same front router without retrieval, only by the conservative variant, and only in some controls.

Everything is a seeded simulation on the g1 fixtures. Nothing is committed and src/*.rs is untouched. No new models or crates were used.

**Deliverables**
- Board entry (VERIFY REQUEST blocks G16-A to G16-D with rerun commands, numbers and negatives): /c/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/results/g16_board_entry.md
- Proposed patch (not applied): /c/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/results/g16_proposed_patch.md
- Bins: src/bin/g16_route.rs, src/bin/g16_retrieval.rs, src/bin/g16_common/mod.rs
- Table printer: py/g16_summary.py
- Results:
  - results/g16_route.{json,log}: tune seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60 on corpus A
  - results/g16_route_confirm.{json,log}: frozen picks, corpus B, seeds 61-90
  - results/g16_picks.json: frozen configs
  - results/g16_retrieval{,_confirm}.{json,log}
  - superseded intermediate runs kept for audit: results/g16_route_v1..v5*

**Worlds**
- Worlds were fixed before any policy ran: sib16, rand16, sib64, mixed50, weakid50 (half the task texts come from a different concept), drift (best-agent table redrawn at task 1000), ctl-irrel (w=0, texts recur but carry no information), ctl-oneoff (w=0, every text a one-off).
- sib64 and ctl-oneoff are never tuned on.

**G16-A: replication check**
- `g16_route --corpus A --check` reproduces g1_route's mini-hybrid arm bit-exactly (max abs difference 5.6e-17).
- The check still passed after the later refactors.

**G16-B: gating, downstream**
- Existing R0 arm vs the same front without retrieval, at H2000 (held-out | confirm):

| World | R0 vs same front |
|---|---|
| sib16 | +.077 \| +.070 |
| rand16 | +.082 \| +.077 |
| ctl-irrel | -.015 \| -.017 (Holm loss) |
| ctl-oneoff | -.016 \| -.020 (Holm loss) |

- Simple confidence gates (a Beta-posterior test against the front's own recent success; also an online logistic gate; also an agreement/margin gate) do not beat R0. They trade recurring-world gain for control safety.
- Mechanism found with a diagnostic run: in the control worlds the votes that fire have mean expected success .46 vs .75 for tasks the front decides.
  - Cause: a flat Beta(1,1) prior lets a lucky streak from a globally mediocre agent qualify (winner's curse).
  - A second cost is the front router's `kn:<anchor>` feature dilution when the feature is injected on every task.
- FINAL arm = anchor evidence shrunk toward the agent's global success rate (kappa 3) + confidence test + the existing window gate kept + `kn:<anchor>` injected only when the vote is open.
- FINAL vs same front, held-out | confirm:

| World | FINAL vs same front |
|---|---|
| sib16 | +.082 \| +.089 |
| rand16 | +.101 \| +.091 |
| sib64 | +.027 \| +.026 |
| drift | +.036 \| +.035 |
| ctl-irrel | -.007 \| -.013 (confirm is a Holm loss) |
| ctl-oneoff | -.011 \| -.013 (Holm loss) |

- FINAL minus R0 is mostly small and not Holm-significant (rand16 +.020 | +.014; sib16 +.006 | +.020, significant only in confirm). Controls improve by about .004-.007.
- Conservative variant (window gate plus confidence test):
  - Controls vs same front: -.003 to -.005, TOST-equivalent within ±.01 in ctl-irrel on both corpora, and in ctl-oneoff on confirm only.
  - Cost: recurring-world gains drop to +.057/+.060 on sib16/rand16, and it is Holm-worse than R0 on sib16 and rand16 in both splits.
- Against the best fair baseline, no arm is equivalent in any control. In controls the best fair baseline is warm(hebr), which is about +.009 above guarded; the vote policies sit on a guarded front.

**G16-C: stage-wise verification**
- Adaptive k downstream: no gain (|d| ≤ .004, not significant).
- Freshness, forced and not tuned:
  - Decay .997 per task hurts: R0 sib16 -.033 | -.029, and the drift world -.010 | -.010 (no gain where the evidence is stale).
  - Reset-after-3-failures is neutral, with a small drift gain on FINAL: +.006 | +.007 at H2000, not significant.
- Spell correction end to end:
  - Spell is the lever: sib16 +.055 and drift +.022 vs raw MiniLM.
  - Hybrid adds nothing beyond spell.
  - Hybrid hurts rand16 by -.032 with thresholds tuned on the panel.
  - BGE ≈ MiniLM-hybrid.

**G16-D: document-level retrieval** (held-out | confirm; confirm for adaptive-k F1 and partition and gate utility, held-out only for dedup tau)
- Adaptive k:
  - Hybrid rankings: +.008 to +.021 F1 over best fixed k.
  - Dense-only rankings: -.03 to -.05 F1 vs fixed k=2.
- Dedup: exact-duplicate suppression (cosine ≥ .999) gives +.021 F1@3 on a store with 30% duplicates. Embedding-cosine detection of superseded revisions fails: the stale-served rate is unchanged.
- Project partitions (pooled vs tag-partitioned, two projects with the same concepts but different answers):
  - Tag-partitioned hit@1 .914 | .920 vs pooled .472 | .480, but this needs a reliable tag.
  - Soft cosine boost is the more robust choice under tag noise.
  - Scan time drops from 771 to 219 microseconds per query.
- Topic-domain partitions (centroid routing within one corpus) lose: hit@1 -.084 for 1 domain, -.015 for 2 domains.
- Retrieval-level abstention gate (learned logistic or margin; labels = top-1 correct):
  - Utility +.029 | +.032 over always-inject.
  - Wrong-inject drops from .120 to .016 (held-out) at about 18% abstention.

**Caveats (all in the board entry)**
- The tuning objective was changed once after the first full run (v1 to v2) to add a control-loss penalty. The change made policies more conservative.
- The final gate family was found by iterating on the tuning panel logs plus a diagnostic run on held-out seeds 31-60 (mechanism only; nothing was tuned on 31-60 or 61-90).
- Corpus B is the same 240 concepts with different phrasing, so it is a text-level replication.
- The duplicates, revisions and second project in G16-D are labels or sibling corpora, not real data.
- Holm families have hundreds of tests (888 in the vs-best-fair family), so many "ns" cells mean underpowered.

**Suggested next step:** pick the front router per world (warm in controls, guarded in recurring worlds) instead of only gating the vote, since the remaining control gap is mostly warm vs guarded.

- `cargo run --release --offline --bin g16_route -- --corpus B --confirm`  (~70 s, frozen picks, seeds 61-90)
- `cargo run --release --offline --bin g16_retrieval` and `... --bin g16_retrieval -- --confirm`  (about 35 s and 25 s)
